candidate_relations.reason: Neurofibromatosis type 1 is a genetic disorder causing tumors of the nervous system, not primarily an expansive lytic bony lesion as described. The clinical presentation of a solitary lytic bony lesion is not typical for NF1.

The clinical record describes an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing, causing proptosis and vision loss, which is characteristic of fibrous dysplasia.

While Langerhans cell histiocytosis can cause lytic bone lesions, it often presents with other systemic symptoms or multifocal lesions, and the chronic 10-year duration with progressive vision loss is less typical for LCH compared to fibrous dysplasia.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Langerhans cell histiocytosis vs. Fibrous dysplasia

candidate_relations.reason: An orbital schwannoma is a nerve sheath tumor, typically presenting as a well-circumscribed mass, not an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the orbital roof and frontal bone.

Meningiomas are tumors of the meninges and can cause hyperostosis (bone thickening) rather than an expansive lytic lesion, although they can involve the orbit. The description of a lytic lesion is not typical for meningioma.

Orbital metastasis is a type of metastatic disease, but the clinical record does not provide information suggestive of a primary malignancy elsewhere, and the 10-year duration is long for most metastases.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Orbital Metastasis as a specific location of Metastatic disease

candidate_relations.reason: Giant cell tumors are aggressive bone tumors, but they are less common in the orbit and the description of an 'expansive lytic bony lesion' is more characteristic of fibrous dysplasia in this context.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Giant cell tumor vs. Fibrous dysplasia

candidate_relations.reason: An orbital fracture is an acute traumatic injury to the bone, not a chronic, progressive expansive lytic lesion of 10 years' duration.
Metastatic disease implies a primary cancer elsewhere, which is not mentioned. The 10-year duration of symptoms is also atypical for most metastatic lesions.
Idiopathic orbital inflammation (orbital pseudotumor) is an inflammatory condition, typically presenting as a soft tissue mass, not an expansive lytic bony lesion.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Idiopathic orbital inflammation vs. Fibrous dysplasia

candidate_relations.reason: Sarcoidosis is a systemic inflammatory disease that can affect the orbit, but it typically causes granulomatous inflammation of soft tissues or bone lesions that are not primarily described as expansive lytic bony lesions in this manner.

Eosinophilic granuloma is a localized form of Langerhans cell histiocytosis. While it can cause lytic bone lesions, the chronic 10-year duration and progressive nature are less typical for EG compared to fibrous dysplasia.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Eosinophilic granuloma as a form of Langerhans cell histiocytosis

candidate_relations.reason: This is a more specific anatomical localization of fibrous dysplasia, which perfectly matches the clinical description of an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing, causing orbital symptoms.
